# `js/consistent-function-scoping`

**No inner function that uses nothing from its outer function**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `checkArrowFunctions` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (moving the function changes where it is defined and what it is named next to, the author's layout) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/consistent-function-scoping` |

## What it checks

A function declared inside another function — a declaration, a `const f = () => …` or a returned function — that refers to no variable, parameter or function of the enclosing function (or the blocks between) is reported at its head: it can live one level up. Callbacks passed as arguments, object values, functions in an immediately invoked function, in a React hook's callback, in a `jest.mock`/`vi.mock` factory, and arrows that use the outer `this` are left alone.

**Why:** A function recreated on every call of its parent costs allocations and hides that it doesn't depend on the parent.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/consistent-function-scoping" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkArrowFunctions` | `boolean` | `true` | check arrow functions as well as function declarations and expressions |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-scoping"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/consistent-function-scoping".options]
checkArrowFunctions = true
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/consistent-function-scoping" = { severity = "error", options = { checkArrowFunctions = false } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `checkArrowFunctions`

*boolean* · default `true`

check arrow functions as well as function declarations and expressions

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-scoping".options]
checkArrowFunctions = false
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/consistent-function-scoping.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### arrows off

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-scoping".options]
checkArrowFunctions = false
```

```js
function make() {
  return (x) => x * 2;
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/consistent-function-scoping" = { options = { checkArrowFunctions = false } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/consistent-function-scoping" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/consistent-function-scoping" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/consistent-function-scoping" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/consistent-function-scoping" = { severity = "warn", options = { checkArrowFunctions = false } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/consistent-function-scoping": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"checkArrowFunctions": false}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/consistent-function-scoping: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/consistent-function-scoping expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/consistent-function-scoping --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/consistent-function-scoping       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/consistent-function-scoping  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                  # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the function to the enclosing scope (often the module), and keep its name.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
function format(items) {
  function pad(text) {
    return text.padStart(4);
  }
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

#### Do

```js
function pad(text) {
  return text.padStart(4);
}
function format(items) {
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
function format(items) {
  function pad(text) {
    return text.padStart(4);
  }
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

#### Do

```jsx
function pad(text) {
  return text.padStart(4);
}
function format(items) {
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
function format(items) {
  function pad(text) {
    return text.padStart(4);
  }
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

#### Do

```ts
function pad(text) {
  return text.padStart(4);
}
function format(items) {
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
function format(items) {
  function pad(text) {
    return text.padStart(4);
  }
  return items.map(pad);
}
```

#### Do

```tsx

  return text.padStart(4);
}
function format(items) {
```
